ANSWER:
`ValidateBundleID` is defined in `pkg/registry/vendor.go` (func `ValidateBundleID`). Making it stricter would propagate to every caller that runs an id through it before touching the filesystem or returning a manifest:

Registry-package entry points (all in `pkg/registry/vendor.go`):
- `ResolveVendorDir(workspace, id)` — validates `id` (line 52) before resolving the install dir.
- `RemoveVendorDir(workspace, id)` — validates `id` (line 69) before the recursive delete.
- `(*Staging).Commit(workspace, id)` — validates `id` (line 153) before moving the staged bundle into place.

Registry client entry points (in `pkg/registry/client.go`):
- `(*Client).Resolve` — via its inner `fetchManifest` closure, which calls `ValidateBundleID(m.ID)` (line 91) on the id decoded from a fetched registry manifest. A manifest whose id newly fails would be refused.
- `(*Client).resolveGitURL` — the git-URL resolution path. It derives `id = owner/repo` from the parsed `github.com/owner/repo` URL and calls `ValidateBundleID(id)` (line 158); a stricter rule would make this git-URL resolution start rejecting owner/repo combinations that previously passed.

(The `TestValidateBundleID` test in `pkg/registry/vendor_test.go` also exercises it directly, but that is a test, not an entry point.)

CONFIDENCE: high
